item.title: GSK China Deal Bepirovirsen
item.description:
• Summary: GSK has struck a deal with a Chinese biotech (Sino Biopharmaceutical) to license bepirovirsen, an antisense oligonucleotide therapy for chronic hepatitis B. The agreement gives GSK global rights to the drug outside of China, while the Chinese partner retains rights in its home market. Bepirovirsen is currently in late-stage clinical trials and has shown promise in achieving functional cure for hepatitis B by reducing viral DNA and surface antigen levels. The deal underscores GSK’s commitment to expanding its infectious disease pipeline.
  • MoAs: Bepirovirsen: Antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) targeting hepatitis B virus RNA, reduces production of viral proteins and inhibits viral replication.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive

item.title: Rare Animal Skin Infection
item.description:
• Summary: The article reports on clusters of a rare skin infection caused by Dermatophilus congolensis in Europe, primarily affecting men who have sex with men (MSM). This zoonotic infection raises public health concerns.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: STAT

item.title: RSV Vaccine R&D
item.description:
• Summary: Advances in RSV vaccine research and development are reviewed, including multiple candidates in late-stage trials targeting older adults and infants.
  • MoAs: Prefusion F protein stabilization, viral vector (e.g., adenovirus), or live-attenuated RSV.
  • Sources: BioSpace
